tier_reason: The README Benchmark section prints recursion-test.cc output with the exact bazel/clang flags for aw-backtrace, libgcc and LLVM libunwind (LD_PRELOAD libunwind.so.1), but it states no CPU model, so the record is not tier A; these are first-party numbers.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Cache-hit microbenchmark (frame pointers on): about 9.0-9.7 ns per unwind step vs libgcc 52.3-58.6 ns and LLVM libunwind 275.9-292.4 ns. With the cache off: 28.6-29.4 ns. With the cache off and -fomit-frame-pointer: 69.5-76.1 ns vs libgcc 121.9-133.6 ns and LLVM libunwind 491.8-525.2 ns. README: libgcc about 5x slower, LLVM libunwind another 5x slower than libgcc.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: CC=clang bazel build -c opt --copt=-ggdb3 --copt=-fno-omit-frame-pointer --copt=-march=native (plus -DTESTING_NO_CACHE and -fomit-frame-pointer variants); clang version not stated
corrections.caveats: No CPU model is stated, so the record is not tier A. The headline microbenchmark is mostly cache hits; the cache-off rows (about 1.8x faster than libgcc) are the fairer comparison for cache-missing workloads. First public release was 2026-09-01; the author says the API is not stable and the library needs glibc 2.35+ and works best on Linux 6.11+ (PROCMAP_QUERY). The baselines are unwinders, not perf, gprof or Valgrind. The author discloses using LLMs during development.

notes: ISC license confirmed from LICENSE (0BSD-like ISC text, Copyright 2026 gperftools Contributors). 3 stars, 72 commits, not a fork; last commit 2026-09-25.

tier_reason: The PR body gives a before/after table for the ClickHouse llvm-project fork's libunwind on a Ryzen 9 7950X3D and Graviton4; the benchmark code is public (src/Common/benchmarks/stack_trace.cpp), but the compiler and flags are not stated in the PR, so the record is first-party tier C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Stack trace capture (45 frames, depth 64): 8594 to 1351 ns (6.36x) on x86-64, 22480 to 3093 ns (7.27x) on AArch64. Exception throw/catch at depth 16: 17418 to 3661 ns (4.76x), 41174 to 7091 ns (5.81x). 32 cache-miss call sites: 10219 to 8687 ns (1.18x), 27147 to 24630 ns (1.10x). Profiler-style signal-handler sample at depth 0: 4384 to 3103 ns (1.41x), 6900 to 3796 ns (1.82x).
corrections.caveats: This is a before/after of the project's own change to its libunwind fork (contrib/llvm-project submodule, https://github.com/ClickHouse/llvm-project): decoded unwind rules are cached by instruction pointer in a lock-free, signal-safe table on Linux x86-64 and AArch64 only. The large wins apply only to repeated stacks; the cache-miss and profiler-sample rows show 1.1-1.8x. The benchmark code is src/Common/benchmarks/stack_trace.cpp (Google Benchmark); the PR states no compiler or flags. The PR, merged 2026-10-01, also fixes a DW_CFA_remember_state stack overflow on fibers. The baseline is the previous libunwind, not perf, gprof or Valgrind; repo_url is the host repo, since the fork itself was not opened.
corrections.stars_or_usage: ClickHouse 50.3k stars; used in ClickHouse's StackTrace, exceptions and query profiler
corrections.license: Apache-2.0 (ClickHouse); the libunwind fork is under Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception (not rechecked)
